quickAnswerTitle: 2026-2027 New York School Calendar Dates at a Glance
quickAnswer: Most New York public schools begin the 2026-2027 school year in September 2026 and end in June 2027, but the exact dates vary by district. NYCPS starts on September 10, 2026 and ends on June 28, 2027; suburban, Long Island, Westchester, and upstate districts may publish different first days, recess weeks, conference days, and last days.

about:
New York public school calendars are approved locally, so there is no single statewide school calendar for every public school family. First day of school, last day, winter recess, midwinter recess, spring recess, staff development days, conference days, religious holidays, Regents administration windows, and emergency closure dates can differ by district. New York City Public Schools is the largest district in the state and publishes a detailed school year calendar for 3-K through grade 12 families.

New York is different from many states because high school families often need to plan around Regents examination periods as well as ordinary school holidays. Regents windows can affect January testing schedules, June attendance patterns, graduation planning, make-up exams, and family travel decisions for students in tested courses. District calendars may mention Regents dates directly, while individual high schools may publish more specific testing schedules.

Calendar patterns also vary by region. NYCPS uses a citywide school calendar with religious holidays, midwinter recess, parent-teacher conference notes, and Regents windows. Long Island, Westchester, and Hudson Valley districts usually publish district-specific calendars approved by local boards. Upstate districts such as Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse, Albany, and others may use different recess patterns, weather make-up plans, and professional development days.

Families should use the district calendar as the source of record for attendance planning, then verify school-level details for parent-teacher conferences, testing, Regents exams, graduation, athletics, transportation, and emergency updates. MySchoolDates organizes available New York district calendar pages and links back to official district sources for final verification.

stateSections.label: New York School Calendar Characteristics
stateSections.content:
New York school calendars are highly local. Families should not assume that NYCPS, Long Island, Westchester, Hudson Valley, and upstate districts share the same first day, February break, spring recess, or last day. This matters for childcare, shared custody schedules, family travel, summer camp planning, and high school testing.

The biggest New York-specific planning issue is Regents testing. Unlike many states, New York high school calendars may be shaped by statewide Regents exam windows in January, June, and August. Students who take Regents exams may have school-specific testing schedules even when younger grades follow a normal attendance pattern.

faqs.q: When do New York schools start?
faqs.a: New York school start dates vary by district. Many districts begin in September, but families should select their district calendar below to confirm the official first day.

faqs.q: Does New York have a statewide school calendar?
faqs.a: No. New York does not publish one statewide K-12 calendar for every public school district. Districts publish and update their own calendars, so families should use the official district calendar for final dates.

faqs.q: How many school districts are in New York?
faqs.a: New York has hundreds of public school districts, and calendar dates are usually set locally. MySchoolDates adds district calendar pages after official district sources have been reviewed.

faqs.q: Where can I find the New York City Public Schools calendar?
faqs.a: Use the New York City Public Schools calendar page on MySchoolDates for NYCPS first day, last day, school closures, recess periods, PDF links, and calendar download options.

faqs.q: Do New York schools have midwinter recess?
faqs.a: Some New York districts, including New York City Public Schools, schedule a February midwinter recess. Check the specific district calendar because not every district uses the same break pattern.

faqs.q: When is spring recess for New York schools?
faqs.a: Spring recess varies by district and school year. Select a district calendar on this page to confirm the official dates.

faqs.q: Do all New York schools have the same spring break?
faqs.a: No. Spring recess dates can differ between NYCPS, Long Island, Westchester, Hudson Valley, and upstate districts because New York school calendars are approved locally.

faqs.q: How many school days are required in New York?
faqs.a: New York schools generally plan calendars to meet state instructional time and attendance requirements, but families should use the official district calendar for the published student-day schedule.

faqs.q: When are New York Regents exams?
faqs.a: Regents exams are typically administered during state-designated windows, including January, June, and August. District and high school calendars should be checked for the specific dates that apply to each student.

faqs.q: When is the NYC school calendar released?
faqs.a: NYCPS releases school-year calendars before the school year begins and may update calendar details when needed. Families should use the NYCPS calendar page and official source links for the latest reviewed dates.

faqs.q: Can I add a New York school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. District pages on MySchoolDates include calendar download options when available, including ICS files that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook.

faqs.q: Where can I download the New York school calendar PDF?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide New York school calendar PDF for every district. Use the verified district calendar page or the official district website to download a printable PDF for your school system.

faqs.q: What are the longest school breaks in New York?
faqs.a: The longest breaks usually include winter recess, spring recess, and in some districts a February midwinter recess. Exact break lengths vary by district, so families should compare the official district calendar before booking travel.
